summary:
Terra Analog is a web platform and mobile application that allows researchers and mission planners to search for and compare locations on Earth that have similar characteristics to the Moon and Mars. The platform uses available NASA databases to allow users to examine an interactive map of locations on Earth that serve as analog sites for [e.g., deserts, volcanic terrain, polar regions] and view their similarity to lunar or Martian conditions in terms of [terrain, temperature, radiation, geology, isolation].

The proposed platform solves the problem by consolidating scattered scientific information into one resource that can be used for filtering analog sites by [criteria]. By comparing various locations on Earth, users can determine which analog will be best suited for constructing or preparing a base.

Such a platform is necessary as the construction of any space base requires extensive research that needs to be done on the ground first. The use of analogs will allow us to experiment with habitats, equipment, and routines of the crews without spending too many resources and risking human lives.

The complete answer is provided below. The only thing missing is the source of elevation data.

---

Methodology

The Terrestrial Analog Finder will give users a ranked list of locations on Earth that best match the terrain profile of lunar south pole sites and well-studied sites on Mars. It will provide reasoning behind the rankings. This is done by comparing 12 reference regions (8 lunar south pole sites: Shackleton rim, Haworth, Malapert massif and 4 mars sites: Jezero, Gale, Meridiani, southern Utopia) to 558 potential analog sites on Earth. These include 20 specific analog sites and 538 grid cells over 12 arid, polar and volcanic regions. 469 sites had complete data while 89 were filtered with a reason provided.

All locations are 12km by 12km windows on a 30m grid. From each window we calculate terrain features: local relief, median slope, P90 slope, roughness, hypsometric integral and slope distribution. Only elevation differences are used meaning there is no mixing of different elevation datum. Any windows with less than 95% valid data are not scored. The weighted distance (with robust scaling) between the reference and candidate site was calculated to provide a score. This distance can be converted into a score using the following equation: S = 100 exp(-D). This score provides a similarity between the sites. If the scores are the same then the score is 100.

Thermal and mineral data (ECOSTRESS and VIIRS for Earth, MGS TES for Mars and LRO Diviner for the Moon) are provided for each candidate site. By default these are given a weight of 0. This ensures the ranking is based purely on the terrain.

Advantages:

All rankings can be explained. Each feature has a table and chart to show why each site has its ranking. Users can change the weighting and filtering criteria and see how this affects the rankings. Hillshade images are provided so users can visually see how similar sites are. The methodology page is live and has sensitivity analysis showing the limitations. The tool helps researchers, students and mission planners decide which sites to test habitats, rovers and crew procedures.

Impact:

Often when choosing an analog site on Earth, sites are chosen due to their popularity or ease. We wanted to ensure this was a data driven decision that could be replicated. This will allow teams to find sites they may not have thought about and provide justification for their choice. The tool can also aid students and the public in understanding why sites can be considered ‘Mars-like.’ or ‘Moon-like’.

Technologies Used:

Pipeline: Python 3.12 (rasterio, pyproj, numpy, pillow)

Backend: FastAPI (Pydantic)

Frontend: React 18 (TypeScript, Vite, Tailwind, Leaflet, Recharts)

Data: [DEM data] (Thermal and mineral data: ECOSTRESS, VIIRS, MGS TES, LRO Diviner)

Storage: JSON and PNG (No Database)

Testing: 78 backend tests, 25 frontend tests

Deployment: Docker Image (Render). Data is included in the image so no external services are required.

Hardware: None

Creativity:

Explanation: Most tools would just provide a list of sites. We provided a reason behind each site’s ranking. Honesty: The score is clearly not a probability. The reasons for filtering sites are provided. The thermal data is provided but not included in the score by default. This ensures results can be replicated. Elevation Data: Only elevation differences are used meaning Earth, Moon and Mars data can all be compared fairly. Interactivity: The map is coloured according to similarity, the compare functionality allows 1 reference and up to 3 candidates to be compared and the weighting can be changed. This turned a static analysis into an interactive tool.

Considerations:

Replicability: By default the ranking is based purely on the terrain. The methodology is fixed and there is no database meaning anyone can replicate the results. Data Quality: Sites must have at least 95% valid data. Filtering reasons are provided. Fairness: Robust scaling ensures outliers do not affect the data. Features are not affected by the elevation data. Time and Resources: The project was completed by two people in a short timeframe. We wanted to ensure the core was reliable and thoroughly tested. Usability: The tool includes loading, empty and error states. There is a fallback for the basemap. Filters can be easily followed by non-experts. Limitations: Sites are 12km windows with 30m resolution. This means this tool only compares the shape of the terrain. It does not provide a full picture of the environment (radiation, atmosphere, regolith chemistry etc.). This is stated clearly on the methodology page.
